issues.body: `fb_distinct` and `_cmd_decide` distinguish routes by `(repo, token)`, but `_supersede_fallback_alert` assumes that a distinct tuple means a distinct issue tracker. If `ALERT_REPO` equals `REGISTRY_REPO` while `ALERT_TOKEN` differs from the ambient fallback token, `_cmd_decide` enumerates the same repository twice. On a still-firing tick, `_upsert_alert` confirms/refreshes the issue through the primary credential, `fb_marker_open` is true from the second enumeration, and `_supersede_fallback_alert` finds and closes that exact same issue through the ambient credential. The run returns success with no open alert for a firing condition. This configuration is explicitly recognized elsewhere by the same-repo redaction logic, so it cannot safely be assumed absent.
issues.fix_hint: Define tracker distinctness by normalized repository identity before enumerating or superseding fallback issues; token differences may affect retry capability but must not make one repository look like two trackers. Add an end-to-end test with `ALERT_REPO == REGISTRY_REPO`, distinct working primary/ambient tokens, an existing open marker, and a still-firing classification, asserting that the sole issue remains open and is not supersede-commented.
issues.title: Same-repository routes can close the only firing alert

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The reconciliation is unsafe for the supported same-repository configuration: route identity includes the token, so two credentials for the registry are treated as two repositories. A still-firing alert can therefore be refreshed and immediately closed as its own supposed fallback duplicate. The new tests cover distinct repositories only and do not expose this no-alert outcome.
